Never really seen a haiku with a comma mid-line before. I like the general tone(?) you're getting across with this, and you do a good job of reinforcing/intensifying that with all three lines. I wouldn't mind seeing more haikus like this, not at all.

I think it's a good subject and a great start. Being single myself, love is one of those questions I always fight against. Do I need to be in love to be happy? What do I have to do to obtain it? How can I keep it? How did I lose it so easily? The questions go on. I have a few points or exercises for revision that you might consider, beginning with writing down your own questions of the sort. Then I'd consider the narrative and the diction: If you prefer to stick to one subject, I personally would aim to replace the second "I" in the first line with an adjective. I'd also consider a stronger verb than "waiting" for added description. By "a love," as well as the overall tone, I am thinking that you mean to convey desperation for love, or to personify desperation. You might consider meditating on "waiting," choosing instead something that conveys more pain or passion. And with so few words, it's very difficult to fit in imagery. You might try to find a verb that also evokes imagery. Lastly, you might reconsider "inside" or "chest" because of their obvious nature. A personified heart obviously beats inside a chest. But what if the chest were a throat, a cave, an onion, a prison, or a womb. While this sort of exaggeration might not be necessary, but it can breed imagery and provide a sort of awareness. Every word revised is an opportunity, and there's no better form on which to practice. I can't wait to see what changes you might make! Thanks for posting!
